answer:
RoG 将知识图用于推理的方式是：先生成由 KG 接地（grounded）的关系路径作为忠实计划，再用这些计划到 KG 中检索有效推理路径，供 LLM 执行推理 [E1, E10]。其规划-检索-推理框架明确“not only retrieve the latest knowledge from KGs but also consider the guidance of KG structure for reasoning and explanations” [E10]。RoG 还通过蒸馏 KG 知识训练模型，并且其规划模块可在推理时与任意 LLM 即插即用 [E1, E10]。

MindMap 则通过 KG prompting，让 LLM 理解 KG 输入，并“infer with a combination of implicit and external knowledge” [E5]；它把图结构转换为 mind map，使 LLM 能结合 KG 中的事实与 LLM 的隐式知识进行图推理 [E2, E7]。MindMap 的结论强调“eliciting the mind map”，即推理路径与 rationale 以图的形式表示 [E8]；其摘要还称方法“reveals their reasoning pathways based on the ontology of knowledge” [E5]。

可解释性结论的边界：RoG 的证据称可基于推理路径提供可解释解释，并在案例中称生成忠实关系路径、检索有效推理路径 [E3]；但其解释性陈述限于所展示案例与作者结论 [E3]。MindMap 的证据称其提升推理透明度、mind map 表示推理路径与 rationale [E5, E8]，但未给出统一的跨数据集可解释性度量；其解释质量评估使用 BERTScore 与 GPT-4 ranking，并指示 GPT-4 优先正确性 [E2]。因此，不能据共同数据集推断二者可解释性可直接比较，原文也未提供同一协议下的胜负证据 [E2]。关于 MindMap 与 RoG 的直接方法对比，现有证据未给出；流程细节上，RoG 有规划-检索-推理描述 [E1, E10]，MindMap 的完整推理流程证据为 KG prompt 与 mind map 描述 [E5, E7]，更细步骤证据不足。

ABSTRACT
Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive reasoning abili-
ties in complex tasks. However, they lack up-to-date knowledge and experience
hallucinations during reasoning, which can lead to incorrect reasoning processes
and diminish their performance and trustworthiness. Knowledge graphs (KGs),
which capture vast amounts of facts in a structured format, offer a reliable source
of knowledge for reasoning. Nevertheless, existing KG-based LLM reasoning
methods only treat KGs as factual knowledge bases and overlook the importance
of their structural information for reasoning. In this paper, we propose a novel
method called reasoning on graphs (RoG) that synergizes LLMs with KGs to
enable faithful and interpretable reasoning. Specifically, we present a planning-
retrieval-reasoning framework, where RoG first generates relation paths grounded
by KGs as faithful plans.

Prompt engineering seeks to improve the capacity of
large large language models (e.g., ChatGPT) in diverse
complex tasks such as question answering, sentiment clas-
sification, and common sense reasoning. Chain-of-thought
(CoT) prompt [63] enables complex reasoning capabilities
through intermediate reasoning steps. Prompt engineering
also enables the integration of structural data like knowl-
edge graphs (KGs) into LLMs. Li et al. [64] simply linearizes
the KGs and uses templates to convert the KGs into pas-
sages. Mindmap [65] designs a KG prompt to convert graph
structure into a mind map that enables LLMs to perform
reasoning on it. Prompt offers a simple way to utilize the
potential of LLMs without finetuning. Proficiency in prompt
engineering leads to a better understanding of the strengths
and weaknesses of LLMs.

Knowledge Graphs (KGs)
Knowledge graphs (KGs) store structured knowledge as a
collection of triples KG = {(h, r, t) ⊆E × R × E}, where E
and R respectively denote the set of entities and relations.
Existing knowledge graphs (KGs) can be classified into four
groups based on the stored information: 1) encyclopedic KGs,
2) commonsense KGs, 3) domain-specific KGs, and 4) multi-
modal KGs. We illustrate the examples of KGs of different
categories in Fig. 5.
